purpose: Ciclesonide is used to help control and prevent asthma symptoms, or to relieve nasal symptoms like stuffiness, runny nose, and sneezing caused by allergies. It does not work right away in an emergency, so it is not a rescue inhaler. It works best when used regularly every day as prescribed.
how_it_works: Ciclesonide is a steroid that reduces swelling and irritation in your airways or nasal passages. Think of it like calming down an overreactive immune response in your nose or lungs. Over time, this makes it easier to breathe and helps prevent allergy or asthma flare-ups.
common_side_effects: Headache, sore throat, or a runny nose are the most common side effects. Some people may notice a mild unpleasant taste or smell after using the nasal spray. Occasionally, it can cause a nosebleed or mild irritation in the throat or mouth.
warnings: Do not use this medicine as a quick-relief inhaler during a sudden asthma attack — always have a fast-acting rescue inhaler on hand. Long-term use of steroids can sometimes affect your immune system, so tell your doctor if you are exposed to chickenpox or measles. Children using this medicine regularly should have their height monitored, as steroid inhalers can occasionally slow growth slightly with long-term use. Do not stop using it suddenly without talking to your doctor.
typical_dosing: For asthma (inhaler): Adults and teens usually take 1-2 puffs once or twice a day, depending on how severe the asthma is. For nasal allergies (nasal spray): Adults and children 6 years and older typically use 1-2 sprays in each nostril once a day. Always follow the exact directions your doctor gives you.
